habitat: Dry mixed bushveld, savanna and thornveld. Pairs, and in winter flocks of up to about 30. Mainly arboreal.
summary: A common bushveld hornbill. The male has a rather small dark bill. The female has a smaller casque, a creamy upper mandible and a red bill tip. Both sexes have a white eyebrow and pale feather edges on the wings. The upperparts are dark grey and the wings are mottled brown, with a cream patch on the bill. The immature has a browner head and indistinct eyebrows. The call is a thin piping series given with the bill pointing skywards.

similar.note: Southern Yellow-billed Hornbill has a large yellow bill and pied plumage. African Grey Hornbill has a small dark or cream-and-red bill and a white eyebrow.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^15=32768 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 16384–65536.

viewNotes.note: White eyebrow, dark grey upperparts and mottled brown wings. The male’s bill is small and dark; the female’s upper mandible is creamy with a red tip.
The white eyebrow and the bill colour separate the sexes from the front.
Dark grey back and pale-edged wings.
Mottled brown wings. A separate upperwing flight pattern was not named.
The underwing colour was not named.

calls.description: A thin, piping, plaintive series, phe, phephee, pheephee, pheeoo, phew, pheeoo-pheeooo, given with the bill pointing skywards. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from Skukuza.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman calls it a common resident and notes winter flocks, which are not an absence. Chick down and a flight photograph are gaps. The call is grade A from Skukuza and is not sexed.
